impact:
ISS-011 replaced the session SWAP panel with ExercisePicker but deliberately left the separate ADD panel alone, so the session screen now has two different idioms for choosing an exercise and one of them still carries the defect ISS-008 fixed in the program builder.

WHERE THE DEFECT IS
- apps/web/src/screens/session/SessionScreen.tsx:862-871 — `library.map(...)` renders every library exercise as a chip with no query input. Past a screenful the rest is unreachable by browsing, and nothing in the 65-entry catalog is reachable at all.
- apps/web/src/screens/session/SessionScreen.tsx:872-888 — a bare name input plus a kind selector, wired to `createAndAdd` (SessionScreen.tsx:289-298). That is the exact-name create ISS-008 replaced: a typo mints a second, untagged library row.

WHERE THE SYMPTOM IS TRIGGERED FROM
The "＋ Add an exercise" / "＋ Add what you did" button, SessionScreen.tsx:891-893. On a freeform session it is the only way to log anything.

THE WORKING COUNTER-EXAMPLE
apps/web/src/components/ExercisePicker.tsx over apps/web/src/lib/exercise-pick.ts, now used by both the program builder and the session swap panel.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED WITH ISS-011
Dropping the picker in here would be a small change except for one regression: KIND_OPTIONS (apps/web/src/components/ExercisePicker.tsx:9-13) offers weighted/reps/time only, while the add panel offers `distance` as well (SessionScreen.tsx:880). A freeform session is where a ride or a run gets logged, so losing `distance` on create would break the case the add panel exists for. Fixing this means deciding whether `distance` joins the picker's kind options — which also changes the program builder — or whether the session add panel keeps its own kind selector beside the picker.

VERIFIED vs SUSPECTED
Verified by reading both files at HEAD after the ISS-011 fix; line numbers checked at time of writing. The unreachability past a screenful is read from the unfiltered `map`, not reproduced against a large library.
title: The session's "Add an exercise" panel still browses unfiltered chips and creates by bare name
